title: TERRAYIELD FARMS
subtitle: Agricultural Brand System
description:
The Quick Snapshot Project  
Type: Self-Initiated Brand Identity Concept  
Industry: Agriculture / Sustainable Farming  
Focus Areas: Visual Strategy, Logo System, Typography, and Packaging Design.  
The Vibe: Authentic, Earthy, Professional, and Sustainable.  

The Backstory (The Problem)  
Agricultural branding often falls into two extremes. It can be overly rustic and "folksy," or it can be stark and corporate. With Terrayield Farms, I aimed to find a middle ground. My goal was to create an identity that feels like a modern partner to the farmer. I wanted it to be professional, reliable, and transparent, while still connecting deeply to the land. I approached this as an exercise in "Elevated Agriculture." I aimed to show that local, sustainable farming can have a visual identity as sophisticated as premium lifestyle brands.  

The Approach  
My process for Terrayield Farms centered around "Grounded Growth."  

The Logo System: I designed the mark to feel structural yet organic. The design emphasizes balance, with clean lines that echo the rows of a field or the geometry of cultivation. I avoided overused, literal clichés like a standard barn or tractor.  

The Palette: The colors draw inspiration from the harvest—deep, rich earth tones alongside fresh, bright greens that signify life and health. This palette feels premium and mature instead of just decorative.  

Typography: I chose a typeface that balances modern readability with a touch of traditional serifs. It’s easy to read on a delivery truck but elegant enough for small labels on artisanal products.  

The Design Decisions (The "Why")  
1. Transparency Through Design  
Because Terrayield Farms focuses on sustainability, I embraced a clean, minimal aesthetic. By incorporating plenty of white space and clear, honest typography, the brand communicates to consumers, "We have nothing to hide; this is a quality product."  

2. Scalable Assets  
A farm brand must work in various settings—from digital social media ads to muddy physical crates and packaging. I designed the brand system to be highly modular, ensuring the logo remains iconic whether it is stamped on raw burlap or printed on a high-resolution marketing flyer.  

The Takeaway  
Terrayield Farms demonstrates that modern design can thrive in traditional industries. By removing unnecessary embellishments and focusing on strong, structural branding, I’ve created an identity built to last. It respects its agricultural roots while confidently looking toward the future of sustainable food.

title: DRIPR
subtitle: Product Design Concept
description:
DRIPR


Project Type: Self-Initiated Product & Packaging Design  
Focus: Packaging aesthetics, label design, print materials, and promotional assets  
Industry: Wellness & Beverage  
The Vibe: Sharp, modern, and high-impact  


The Concept (The Product)  

DRIPR isn’t just a drink; it’s an experience. The goal of this project was to design the product's "face"—the label and the promotional materials. In a competitive market, a product needs to do more than just sit on a shelf. It needs to signal its purpose instantly. I designed DRIPR to cut through the visual clutter of standard beverage aisles by using bold, clean typography and a confident, minimalist layout that tells the consumer exactly what they are getting at a glance.  

The Approach  

My process focused on how a customer experiences the product:  

Packaging & Label Design: I viewed the label as a functional piece of art. The design uses modern typography and a high-contrast palette to create a distinct "shelf presence." Every element—from the hierarchy of product information to the logo placement—was chosen to make the product feel premium and purposeful in the consumer’s hand.  

Promotional Design: The supporting flyers were created to extend the packaging. They share the same visual style, ensuring that whether a customer sees the bottle or a promotional poster, the "DRIPR" look remains clear.  

Holistic Cohesion: The project’s key focus was making sure the packaging and marketing materials felt like one unified system. If the design on the bottle doesn’t match the design on the ad, the message gets lost.  


Why It Works  

This project succeeds because it relies on visual clarity. By removing unnecessary design elements, I let the product’s identity speak for itself. The result is a clean, bold system that looks ready for retail, feels professional, and makes a strong impression the moment it’s picked up.

title: MIKITA
subtitle: Fine Jewelry Brand Identity & Concept
description:
Brand Identity Concept  

MIKITA, Held in Elegance The Quick Snapshot  
Project Type:  
Self-Initiated Brand Identity Concept  

Industry

Fine / Luxury Jewelry  
Focus Areas:  
Logo design, color theory, brand voice, packaging mockups, and campaign art direction.  
The Vibe: Intimate, poetic, calm, and quietly confident.  
The Backstory (The Concept) 
Every piece of jewelry carries a story, but I wanted to focus on the feeling of wearing it instead of just the price. I aimed to design a concept for a luxury jewelry brand called MIKITA. This brand is based on the idea of "holding what matters," meaning that personal adornments serve as anchors for our memories, emotions, and identity. Since this was a self-initiated project, I didn’t have a client setting the rules. I created a brief for myself to develop a premium, high-end identity that felt warm and approachable, rather than cold, intimidating, or overly flashy.  

The Visual Identity  
1. The Logo & Mark  
The Symbol: At the center of the circular badge is a hand-sketched open shell cradling a delicate pearl. The shell represents protection, intimacy, and natural beauty. The pearl embodies timeless elegance.  
The Layout: The circular stamp design gives it a classic, heritage feel. I designed two primary variations: a soft dusty-rose version on an off-white base and a rich, moody plum version for darker applications. This ensures versatility across different mediums.  
2. Color Palette & Typography  
The Palette: MIKITA’s palette balances moody depth with gentle warmth. It features:  
- Deep plum/charcoal (for grounding)  
- Dusty rose and soft mauve (for femininity and emotion)  
- Cream and muted gold (for luxury and softness)  
The Type: I paired a graceful, high-contrast serif font (Comorant Garamond) with ample open space. This allows the typography to feel sophisticated and editorial without overwhelming the reader.  

Brand Personality & Voice  
To ensure the brand felt like a fully realized world, I outlined its core pillars:  
Keywords: Minimal, Timeless, Intimacy, Emotional Value, Elegance, and Soft Power.  
Tone of Voice: Calm, confident, and slightly poetic. The guiding principle for MIKITA’s copy is to avoid being loud or salesy. It invites customers in rather than pushing a product on them.  
Campaign & Packaging Applications  
To illustrate how the brand exists in the real world, I created a few mockups and campaign drafts:  
1. Art Direction & Campaign Visuals  
The photography focuses on natural, soft lighting, delicate fabrics like tulle and silk, and earthy elements such as feathers and shells. The posters feature the headline "Held in Elegance," seamlessly integrating the logo and vertical text layouts for a high-end magazine or editorial feel.  
2. Packaging Design  
The unboxing experience aims for a gentle reveal. The jewelry box is a clean, textured beige/cream with the MIKITA wordmark subtly embossed in gold, accompanied by a rich velvet pouch. The shopping bag follows the same minimalist, tactile aesthetic, featuring premium twisted rope handles and clean, understated branding.  
The Takeaway  
MIKITA was an excellent exercise in restraint. It shows that luxury doesn’t need loud neon colors, heavy drop shadows, or aggressive marketing to feel premium. By using soft textures, elegant typography, and a very human, emotional narrative, this concept effectively bridges the gap between high-end appeal and everyday accessibility. It serves as a solid, evocative draft that clearly communicates to potential clients how their brand stories can be brought to life with grace and clarity.
